items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1983-05-28
items.q: It may have just been that they were auditioning for you and Oren, maybe. I don't think so.

ctx.x: That sounds like Emil Barnes' band auditioning in the back of the record shop.

You don't remember when that was. That would have been in, yes, I can. I do remember. That would probably have been in, after the first of the year, well, let's say spring of 1950. 1950 would be my guess. And who were they auditioning for? I don't know who it was. They were auditioning for somebody. It may have just been that they were auditioning for you and Oren, maybe. I don't think so. There was somebody they were auditioning for, but I don't remember the name. I think they auditioned once for Myron. That may…
Ralston was there one time when they auditioned. Sounds right. And, of course, he was always taking pictures. When he had any opportunity, he was dedicated to that.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: I didn't I didn't know Orrin actually until you and I met later on yeah that would have been October I think

ctx.x: well the reason I think we probably were aware of Raymond at least in my case was that uh Orrin Blackstone had told me about him because Raymond was on the very first issue of playback magazine which Orrin put out now you may never have seen that issue no I didn't see the Raymond Raymond you know he yeah Orrin was very interested in Raymond and uh felt that he was one of the unsung heroes and we had that record of slow blues around that Raymond put out himself

I remember the record vaguely and I remember it being good but yeah I didn't I didn't know Orrin actually until you and I met later on yeah that would have been October I think in fact the only thing I think it would have been the only thing I knew of Orrin at that point was I had read in an article I think in the 1945 Esquire jazz book meant an article on collecting records uh describing Orrin's findings in very rare records in junk shops and I was impressed enough that I would not have begun to approach him…

mm-hmm well I thought that gee I guess I met Orrin in 1945 he just opened up the shop and it would have been probably in the summer I'd have to think about my navy days and when I went in and because I was extremely young I would have been 18 years old like 18 yeah 18 years old and uh yeah our birthdays are within a month of each other so so we're about to now I ought to yeah anyway but anyway uh and somehow I had been reading down downbeat and had gotten very uh that's something we haven't mentioned at all…
